gameOver.message: Player o3 Worrier is the winner

annotations.description: Playing Scrubland as the first land instead of Karakas is debatable. Karakas is a legendary land that can bounce legendary creatures (including the opponent's potential Marit Lage or other legendary threats) and also bounces your own Solitude for repeated use. Since Aether Vial only costs {1} generic mana, Karakas could have been played to cast Aether Vial while preserving the dual lands for future color needs. However, Scrubland provides both white and black mana which gives more flexibility for casting spells like Lively Dirge or hardcasting Solitude later, and Karakas only produces white. The Karakas line is likely better in Legacy where legendary creatures and Karakas's bounce ability are highly relevant, but this is close enough to be debatable rather than a clear mistake.
annotations.actionTaken: Played Scrubland as the first land drop and cast Aether Vial.
annotations.betterLine: Play Karakas first (still casts Aether Vial for {1}), preserving dual lands for later color needs while having Karakas's legendary creature bounce ability available immediately.

annotations.description: Fetched a second Scrubland instead of a basic Swamp. In Legacy, playing around Wasteland is critical. With Scrubland already on battlefield and Savannah + Karakas in hand for future land drops, a basic Swamp would provide the same B mana needed for Orcish Bowmasters this turn and Overlord of the Balemurk's impending cost later, while being immune to Wasteland. Having two nonbasic lands vulnerable to Wasteland is unnecessarily risky.
annotations.actionTaken: Fetched Scrubland (second copy) with Marsh Flats
annotations.betterLine: Fetch a basic Swamp to play around Wasteland while still having access to B mana for Bowmasters and future plays, with W mana covered by existing Scrubland and Savannah in hand.

annotations.description: With Recruiter of the Guard's ETB trigger, the player searched for Stoneforge Mystic. While Stoneforge is a strong card in general, the board state shows no Equipment in the deck list that would be immediately impactful, and the player has Overlord of the Balemurk in hand (a 5-drop) with only 3 lands in play. Meanwhile, the opponent is on a combo deck (Balustrade Spy/Undercity Informer/Lively Dirge style) that exiled Elvish Spirit Guide turn 1 and cast Thoughtseize. Flickerwisp could have been searched instead to flicker the Aether Vial (resetting counters isn't great) or more importantly to flicker Recruiter of the Guard for additional value next end step, or to serve as a 3/1 flier for pressure. Phelia, Exuberant Shepherd is another strong option that provides repeated exile/value effects and can be vialed in at 2 counters. However, Stoneforge into Lion Sash (which is in the card reference) provides graveyard hate against what appears to be a graveyard-based combo deck, which is a reasonable line. The choice is defensible but debatable.
annotations.actionTaken: Searched for Stoneforge Mystic with Recruiter of the Guard's ETB
annotations.betterLine: Flickerwisp might have been stronger here for tempo and to flicker Recruiter for another search, or Phelia for repeated exile pressure. Stoneforge is reasonable if the plan is to find Lion Sash for graveyard hate, but that requires additional mana investment over multiple turns against a combo opponent.

annotations.description: Evoked Solitude with no enemy creatures on the battlefield, sacrificing both Solitude and Phelia (pitched as the white card) for zero effect. The opponent is at 3 life with no creatures, and o3 already has 4+ power of attackers that will untap next turn for lethal.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Solitude with Evoke, exiling Phelia from hand, targeting nothing meaningful with no enemy creatures on board.
annotations.betterLine: Simply pass and attack for lethal next turn with the existing board (Bowmasters 1/1 + Orc Army 2/2 + Recruiter 1/1 = 4 damage vs 3 life). Save Solitude and Phelia for potential interaction if needed.

annotations.description: o3 Worrier is already attacking for lethal (10+ damage against 3 life) and needlessly evokes Solitude by exiling White Orchid Phantom from hand. This wastes a card for no benefit since the attack is already lethal without Solitude.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Solitude with Evoke, exiling White Orchid Phantom from hand, during combat when already attacking for lethal damage.
annotations.betterLine: Simply let combat damage resolve for the kill without spending any additional resources. White Orchid Phantom could have been relevant if somehow the game continued.
